title: Unit 04: Book-II Heroes Part 1 (First Year at Harrow, Hitch-Hiking Sahara)
subject: english-12

questions.question: In 'First Year at Harrow', what was Sir Winston Churchill's chief complaint regarding school examiners?

options.A: They always asked questions in his favorite subjects such as history, poetry, and essay writing.
options.B: They invariably tried to expose what he did NOT know (Latin and mathematics) rather than what he knew.
options.D: They graded papers based on physical appearance.

questions.explanation: Churchill humorously observes that examiners had a perverse passion for quizzing him on Greek and Latin, revealing his ignorance instead of testing his broad historical knowledge.

questions.question: How did young Churchill perform on the Latin entrance examination at Harrow?

options.A: He scored the highest marks in school history.
options.B: He wrote his name, put down the number of the question '(1)', drew brackets, added ink blots, and surrendered a completely blank page.
options.C: He translated Virgil into rhyming English couplets.
options.D: He answered only the historical footnotes.

questions.explanation: For two hours, Churchill sat gazing at his Latin paper, managing only to write his name, a bracketed number, and several blotches of ink.

questions.question: Why did Headmaster Mr. Welldon accept Churchill into Harrow despite his blank Latin paper?

options.A: Churchill's father was Lord Randolph Churchill, Chancellor of the Exchequer.
options.B: Mr. Welldon took a broad, discerning view of Churchill's general intellect and character beyond mere classical rote learning.
options.C: Churchill paid a bribe to the proctors.
options.D: The Latin paper was misplaced by examiners.

questions.explanation: Churchill credits Mr. Welldon with extraordinary discernment for judging his underlying ability rather than rejecting him for a blank paper.

questions.question: What unexpected academic advantage did Churchill gain by being placed in the lowest academic division at Harrow?

options.A: He was excused from all military drills.
options.B: While clever boys studied Latin and Greek, he was taught English language and grammar thoroughly by an exceptional teacher, Mr. Somervell.
options.C: He was permitted to leave school two years earlier.
options.D: He spent all his time playing polo.

questions.explanation: Because he was considered a dunce, Churchill had to master English grammar thoroughly—parsing sentences into color-coded parts—giving him command of prose.

questions.question: What famous incident occurred at the Harrow swimming pool involving Churchill and Leo Amery?

options.A: Churchill challenged Amery to a swimming marathon.
options.B: Seeing a small boy from behind, Churchill playfully shoved him into the pool, only to discover Amery was a senior gymnast and Head of House.
options.D: They organized a boy strike at the baths.

questions.explanation: Churchill pushed small-statured senior boy Leo Amery into the water as a prank, leading to a hasty, clever apology: 'My father, who is a great man, is also small!'

questions.question: In 'Hitch-Hiking across the Sahara', who was the adventurous young American traveler?

options.A: Robert Christopher
options.B: Alexander Fleming

questions.explanation: Robert Christopher set out to hitch-hike across the immense, blistering Sahara desert from North Africa to Timbuktu.

questions.question: What was the total distance of the trans-Saharan crossing undertaken by Christopher?

options.A: About 3,200 kilometers (2,000 miles) across desert wasteland
options.B: Around 500 kilometers along paved highways

questions.explanation: The Sahara crossing from Algiers to Gao covered over 2,000 miles (3,200 km) of desert sands and scorching rock plateaus.

questions.question: At what desert outpost did Christopher have to wait weeks before finding a south-bound transport truck?

options.A: In Salah / El Golea
options.B: Cairo

questions.explanation: Christopher journeyed through oasis outposts like El Golea, In Salah, and Tamanrasset, enduring scorching weeks waiting for military convoys.

questions.question: What extreme temperature is recorded during summer days in the central Sahara as described in the essay?

options.A: Upwards of 130°F (54°C) in the shade
options.B: Around 90°F

questions.explanation: The blazing sun drove midday temperatures to 130°F (54°C), making metal truck bodies hot enough to fry an egg and boiling water in canteens.

questions.question: When Christopher and his companions ran out of drinking water in the blistering wasteland, what desperate measure saved their lives?

options.A: Digging deep artesian wells by hand in two minutes
options.B: Draining the rusty, oily, scalding water from the truck's engine radiator and filtering it through a cloth to drink
options.D: Summoning a helicopter via satellite phone

questions.explanation: They drained foul, oily boiling water from the radiator, allowing it to cool and settle before desperately drinking it to avoid death by dehydration.

questions.question: What nomadic Berber tribe inhabits the Hoggar mountains of the central Sahara, known as the 'Veiled Men' of the desert?

options.A: The Tuareg
options.B: The Bedouin of Arabia

questions.explanation: The Tuareg warriors wear indigo tagelmusts (face veils) covering their mouths and noses to protect against desert glare and sandstorms.

questions.question: In 'First Year at Harrow', what was Churchill's view on teaching foreign languages in British schools?

options.A: All boys should learn Greek before learning English.
options.B: Boys should learn English first, thoroughly and well; then clever boys might learn Latin as an honor and Greek as a treat.
options.C: English should be abolished from public schools.
options.D: Foreign languages should be banned by law.

questions.explanation: Churchill famously said: 'I would make them all learn English; and then I would let the clever ones learn Latin as an honour, and Greek as a treat.'

questions.question: How did Christopher survive a fierce sandstorm (simoom) in the open desert?

options.A: By running toward the oasis
options.B: By lying flat under a heavy blanket behind the vehicle's tires, breathing through cloth to avoid suffocating on flying sand

questions.explanation: During a simoom, blinding sand tears skin and suffocates lungs; travelers must lie prone and cover their faces until the gale subsides.

questions.question: What is the ultimate destination that Christopher reached on the Niger River at the conclusion of his trans-Saharan trek?

options.A: Gao and Timbuktu
options.B: Johannesburg

questions.explanation: Christopher safely navigated the desert and reached Gao on the Niger River, continuing on to ancient Timbuktu.

questions.question: In Churchill's essay, what does the word 'discernment' mean regarding Headmaster Welldon?

options.A: Physical athletic fitness
options.B: The ability to judge well, perceive depth of character, and see beyond superficial appearances

questions.explanation: 'Discernment' is the faculty of penetrating perception, deep insight, and wise evaluation.

questions.question: What was the psychological toll of mirages on desert travelers as experienced by Christopher?

options.A: They provided real fresh water to drink.
options.B: They created cruel optical illusions of glistening blue lakes and palm groves that vanished upon approach, intensifying mental despair.

questions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction creates false images of water bodies, tormenting exhausted travelers with illusory hope.

questions.question: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: 'Churchill's *broad-minded* headmaster recognized his potential.'

options.A: Compound adjective
options.B: Abstract noun

questions.explanation: 'Broad-minded' is a hyphenated compound adjective modifying the noun 'headmaster'.

questions.question: What happened to Christopher's companion truck in the shifting sand dunes?

options.A: It flew over the dunes with ease.
options.B: Its heavy wheels sank up to the axles in loose, powdery fesh-fesh sand, requiring hours of digging and steel tracks to free.

questions.explanation: Sand dunes trap heavy trucks; crew and passengers must shovel hot sand and place steel ladder tracks under spinning wheels.

questions.question: What was Churchill's position on the traditional roll-call at Harrow?

options.A: He was called first because his name was Winston.
options.B: He was summoned almost last because boys were called alphabetically, and his name began with 'S' (Spencer-Churchill), placing him at the bottom of the list.

questions.explanation: Spencer-Churchill put him near the very end of the roll-call, making his bottom academic rank visible to the entire school.

questions.question: What is the synonym of 'arduous' as applied to Christopher's desert journey?

options.A: Effortless and breezy
options.B: Demanding, exhausting, and filled with great exertion

questions.explanation: 'Arduous' means requiring strenuous effort, difficult, and physically taxing.

questions.question: Why did Christopher decide to travel on a camel for a segment of the desert?

options.A: Because motorized trucks could not navigate the steep, broken boulder fields of the Ahaggar mountains
options.B: Because camels are faster than airplanes
options.C: Because trucks were illegal in Africa
options.D: To race against the French Foreign Legion

questions.explanation: Where wheel tracks ceased in mountainous boulder terrain, camels were the only reliable means of transport.

questions.question: In 'First Year at Harrow', Mr. Somervell taught English analysis using what innovative method?

options.A: He made boys write Shakespeare plays from memory.
options.B: He divided long sentences into subject, verb, and object using different colored inks (black, red, blue, green).
options.C: He played phonograph recordings in class.
options.D: He gave tests exclusively in Latin.

questions.explanation: Mr. Somervell used a visual structural system with colored inks and brackets, making sentence syntax intuitively understandable.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to throw someone in at the deep end'?

options.A: To teach swimming by professional coaches
options.B: To push someone into a complex, difficult situation or responsibility without adequate preparation or help
options.C: To throw money into a fountain

questions.explanation: The idiom means forcing someone to face a daunting challenge immediately with no gradual training.

questions.question: What lesson does Churchill draw from his school experience at Harrow?

options.A: That school prizes always predict later success in life.
options.B: That early academic failure in classical examinations does not preclude brilliant literary, political, and national leadership.
options.C: That everyone should abandon reading books.
options.D: That examinations should be decided by lottery.

questions.explanation: Churchill became a Nobel laureate in Literature and Prime Minister of Great Britain despite failing entrance exams.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelled word:

options.A: Discernment
options.B: Descernment

questions.explanation: 'Discernment' is spelled with 'sc' and 'ernment'.

questions.question: What is 'fesh-fesh' in Saharan geography as experienced by Christopher?

options.A: Deep underground freshwater springs
options.B: A fine, treacherous dust that looks solid but collapses under weight like quicksand
options.C: A type of date palm fruit
options.D: A hot green tea served by Tuaregs

questions.explanation: 'Fesh-fesh' is powdered desert dust beneath a deceptive crust that easily traps heavy vehicles.

questions.question: In Churchill's essay, why did he say he would whip boys 'only for not knowing English'?

options.A: Because he believed mastery of one's mother tongue is essential for clear thought and civic leadership.
options.B: Because he despised all foreign cultures.
options.C: Because he wanted to be an authoritarian schoolmaster.

questions.explanation: Churchill viewed mastery of the English language as the primary instrument of clear expression and effective governance.

questions.question: What was the psychological impact of the endless Saharan horizon on Christopher?

options.A: An acute feeling of insignificance and vulnerability under an immense, merciless sky
options.B: A sense of urban claustrophobia
options.D: A feeling that he was in New York City

questions.explanation: The boundless, featureless sands create a profound sensation of human frailty against the colossal forces of nature.

questions.question: Identify the voice of the sentence: 'A heavy load of books was carried across the river by Squire.'

options.A: Active Voice
options.B: Passive Voice

questions.explanation: The subject ('load') receives the action ('was carried') from the agent introduced by 'by', defining passive voice.

questions.question: What emergency fuel or water source did Christopher's convoy rely upon when stranded?

options.A: Melting plastic bottles
options.B: The radiator reserve tank of the convoy truck

questions.explanation: The radiator reserve was the only liquid left between the stranded men and death by dehydration.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'inauspicious' in describing Christopher's start?

options.A: Promising great success and fortune
options.B: Unfavorable, unpromising, or suggesting bad luck ahead

questions.explanation: 'Inauspicious' means boding ill, unpromising, or accompanied by negative omens.

questions.question: How did Churchill view his fellow Harrow classmates who had won prizes in Latin and Greek in their adult lives?

options.A: They became the sole rulers of the world.
options.B: Many had to learn ordinary English afterwards to earn their living or make their way in politics, proving his training was superior.

questions.explanation: In adult life, those who shone in Latin and Greek had to master practical English to communicate in the real world.

questions.question: What animal provided milk and nourishment during Christopher's stay with the Tuaregs?

options.A: Desert camels and goats
options.B: Water buffaloes

questions.explanation: Tuaregs survive on camel milk and cheese, perfectly adapted to the arid desert biosphere.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: He is one of those men who is always ready to help.
options.B: He is one of those men who are always ready to help.
options.C: He is one of those man who are always ready to help.
options.D: He is one of those men who am always ready to help.

questions.explanation: The relative clause 'who are always ready to help' modifies the plural antecedent 'men', requiring a plural verb.

questions.question: What key virtue unites Churchill at Harrow and Christopher in the Sahara?

options.A: Indomitable courage, perseverance, and resilience in the face of daunting adversity
options.B: Immense hereditary financial wealth

questions.explanation: Both essays showcase indomitable perseverance—Churchill overcoming academic stigma and Christopher conquering the deadly Sahara.
